chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said:

I was with Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) in a corner of the Sacred Mosque, and a group of people were reciting the Talbiyyah around the Ka'bah. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you see these who are reciting the Talbiyyah? By Allah, their voices are more hateful to Allah than the voices of donkeys.'

key_terms.يُلَبُّونَ: Reciting the Talbiyyah (the ritual proclamation during Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq say about the voices of those reciting Talbiyyah around the Ka'bah?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) critiques the superficiality of the pilgrims' recitation of the Talbiyyah, comparing their noisy, perhaps distracted or insincere, voices to the braying of donkeys. This highlights the Shia emphasis on *khushu'* (humility and presence of heart) over mere mechanical ritualism, a theme central to the *Mu'tamarat* (miscellaneous) chapter. The critique serves as a reminder that the spiritual efficacy of Hajj depends on the quality of devotion rather than the volume of recitation.
